children: Our Bureau Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court has quashed a 482.70 crore penalty slapped by the state government over limestone mining operations in Kalaburagi district on cement major ACC , in a major relief to the Adani Group company. A division bench of Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice KS Hemaleka also directed the Department of Mines and Geology to restore the cement maker's full access to the Integrated Lease Management System (ILMS) portal.

In its 89-page judgement, delivered on September 8 and up on the court website now, the bench ordered the state to execute a supplementary lease deed extending ACC's mining rights without insisting on a "no-dues certificate", and to refund the amount deposited by the company under earlier interim court orders. ACC holds a captive mining lease in the state for limestone and shale, which was renewed periodically until February 18, 2023. The company & the department had been locked in a dispute over royalty calculations and estimated output. While the government applied a fixed 1:1.42 limestone-to-clinker formula to calculate extraction, ACC argued that royalties must be assessed on actual weighment data.

title: Karnataka HC Quashes State's 482 cr Mining Penalty on ACC
